title: Workflows, agents, and who owns the control flow

items.stem: A booking handler runs this Python every time: the model extracts machine and time from the student's message, the code calls check_calendar, the code calls book_slot if the slot is free, and the model writes the confirmation. Which label fits, and why?

options.text: An agent, because the model is called twice and tools are used
A workflow, because the code fixes the order of the steps
An agent, because it books equipment for the student on its own
A workflow, because no step calls a tool or a model

items.stem: Your code is `while steps < 10: reply = call_model(messages, tools); if no tool requested: break; result = run_tool(reply); messages.append(result); steps += 1`. After each tool result, what decides which tool runs next: the model or the code?

A job runs at 2 a.m.: for each student whose safety training expires within 7 days, read their record, have the model write a one-paragraph reminder, and send it. The steps never change, the budget is small, and failures must be easy to debug. Which design is best for those constraints?

options.text: One agent with query, draft and send tools, choosing its own order each night
Several cooperating agents, one per step, passing messages to each other
An agent now, since it can cope with any change to the job later
Plain code looping over students, with one model call to write each reminder

items.stem: Handling one request costs 2 model calls as a fixed workflow, or on average 5 model calls as an agent. Assume every call costs $0.002 and the assistant gets 10,000 requests a month. How many more dollars per month does the agent design cost than the workflow?
Which of these makerspace requests is the best fit for an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Book the laser cutter for Friday at 3 pm and email a confirmation
Say how thick the acrylic can be on the laser cutter
Book the earliest slot this week where a 3D printer and a staff member are both free
Remind a student that their training expires next week

items.stem: Your booking code always runs check_calendar, then book_slot. One day the calendar replies "laser cutter under maintenance". Without anyone writing new code for that case, which design could try another machine on its own: the workflow as written, or an agent?
